runner.tool_cache_note: host-local and gitignored; only its HASHES are tracked

frozen_stream.why: C1: first candidate in cell (0,0) -- new cell
C1: first candidate in cell (1,0) -- new cell
C2 setup: same cell as id 10, HIGHER objective -> replaces 10
C3: same cell, LOWER objective than incumbent 12 -> rejected
C4 tie: same cell as id 11, EXACTLY equal objective
C1: new cell (3,2) -- equal objective, DIFFERENT cell, both kept

sequential_add_result.why: C1: first candidate in cell (0,0) -- new cell
C1: first candidate in cell (1,0) -- new cell
C2 setup: same cell as id 10, HIGHER objective -> replaces 10
C3: same cell, LOWER objective than incumbent 12 -> rejected
C4 tie: same cell as id 11, EXACTLY equal objective
C1: new cell (3,2) -- equal objective, DIFFERENT cell, both kept

cases.claim: a candidate landing in an empty cell is retained with status 2 (new cell)
id 12 (obj 2.0) replaces incumbent id 10 (obj 1.0) in cell (0,0)
id 13 (obj 0.5) is rejected against incumbent id 12 (obj 2.0)
an EXACTLY equal objective does NOT displace the incumbent, because insertion requires strictly greater than the cell threshold and the default threshold is the incumbent's own objective
cases.consequence_for_h3: First-writer-wins on exact ties. Any H3 retention policy that expects last-writer-wins on ties is NOT what this archive does, and a policy comparison that does not state this is measuring the archive's default alongside its own rule.

cases.claim: upstream documents first-in-batch winning an exact tie; measured here
every retained candidate sits in the cell computed by hand from the measures and the declared 4x4 tessellation over [0,1]^2
retained ids under sequential insertion are exactly the hand-computed set
the identical stream inserted into a second fresh archive retains the identical ids, for both granularities
batch and one-at-a-time insertion of the IDENTICAL stream retain the same ids on THIS stream -- which is a statement about this stream, not a general equivalence
cases.scope_limit: The two granularities agree here because every collision in this stream resolves the same way under 'max of batch' and under 'sequential strictly-greater'. A stream where a LOW candidate precedes a HIGH one in the same cell could differ in reported STATUS even when the retained set matches. H3 should declare its granularity rather than rely on this agreement.

cases.claim: the retention check inserts a frozen stream directly; no emitter object and no scheduler object is ever constructed
cases.module_presence_is_not_the_gate: `import ribs.archives` eagerly imports the emitters and schedulers packages (28 modules on ribs 0.12.0). A gate on module presence is unreachable and was replaced by this instance-level gate after measuring that.
cases.why: An emitter would GENERATE candidates from the archive's own state, which would make the stream a function of the retention policy under test -- the control drawn from the treatment's own selection relation.

design_requirement: identical frozen stream inserted directly into archives, no emitters or schedulers, known collision and tie outcomes, identical retained ids
manifest_first_useful_check: the identical stream inserted directly into archives, no emitters or schedulers, known collision and tie outcomes, identical retained ids under the declared adapter
named_consumer: H3 retention-policy replay (Archaeon's H3 alpha): four retention policies replayed offline over one frozen candidate stream

budget_profile.purpose: run a first-useful-check or a reproduction fixture against ALREADY acquired bytes.
budget_profile.network: FORBIDDEN -- enforced by the check harness, which asserts no acquisition step runs under this profile
budget_profile.rationale: Scientific execution uses already-available inputs and dependencies. A check that needs the network is an acquisition step wearing a check's name.
budget_profile.name: offline_check

resource_receipt.network_policy: FORBIDDEN -- enforced by the check harness, which asserts no acquisition step runs under this profile
resource_receipt.rss_enforcement: NOT ENFORCED -- no job object / cgroup cap. peak_rss_bytes_os_counter is the OS peak-working-set counter for this process and IS reliable; rss_ceiling_exceeded_during_sampling is sampled and can miss a spike. Neither stops a step.
resource_receipt.rss_excludes_children: This is THIS process only. pip, git and venv run as children and their RSS is NOT included.
